key_insight: A reset-free LUCI error-correction design can suppress logical errors on IBM hardware even with nearly half the syndrome density in time.
engineering_relevance: This suggests hardware-friendly quantum codes can trade some temporal distance for flexibility, reduced circuit rigidity, and better tolerance to noisy components.
method: Benchmark a reset-free LUCI framework on IBM quantum hardware.
Asymmetrically scale X or Z code distance to target specific logical Pauli errors.
Compare against the standard rotated surface code under reduced syndrome extraction density.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports logical error suppression ratios of 1.75(10) for X and 1.93(12) for Z in LUCI, versus 1.58(13) and 2.44(7) for the standard approach.
watch_item: The approach requires two subroutine rounds for full syndrome extraction, so reduced temporal distance and added scheduling complexity may limit practical deployment.
paper_title: LUCI on IBM Hardware: Error Suppression with Almost Half Syndrome Density
